notes.title: Iron Mandate - A Post Mortem
notes.content:
TL;DR: Because of a lack of time, money and fundamental issues with the core idea, I'm moving this game out of early access, leaving it free and moving on. If you want to learn more about the reasons and the process of making this game, keep reading. 

Why I'm writing this
I've wanted to write this post mortem for a while now. I was finally moved to do it for two reasons: the first is that I have put this on hold for a while to work on another game: The people of Sea, Sun & Salt. The second is that an alert now appears on the steam page mentionning the fact that it has not received any updates in the past 23 months. It's entirely fair of Steam but I don't want to give the impression that this is some abandonned game. It is fully functional and completable as it is. This pushes me to release it but I don't want to do so without an explanation.

So here we are.

I'm still very proud of the project and I think it is a fun experimental game. I'm so happy that tens of thousands of players have had the chance to try my game.

Unfortunately the game fails in fundamental ways that make it hard to fix. I'll go over some of these reasons and then try to imagine a better version of this game.

https://shared.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2198030/extras/laser-showcase1.gif?t=1679689109

Great idea, failed execution?
The starting point of the project will sound a bit silly: This scene in the opening of Dune (2021). I get that it's entirely missing the point of the shot but seeing it made me think "I want to make a game where a scene like this happens".

I knew I wouldn't be able to do anything in 3D so I focused my thinking on a 2d game. I also wanted it to be a roguelike. I workshopped the idea and I landed on giant mechanical worms firing missiles from side cannons, similar to pre-modern warships.

It's a perfect idea, an awesome concept but I had to ruin it by actually trying to implement it.

https://shared.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2198030/extras/ultimate-showcase2.gif?t=1679689109

Failure 1: Controls
It is just very hard to get used to the controls. There is no singular intuitive way to control the worm so the early part of the game is inevitably this clunky experience of slowly grasping movement.

The player barely has time to understand movement before they have to figure out targetting and weapon control.

It's a mess. You can get through it but by that point so much goodwill was lost and a lot of players will drop out.

I tried to give move control options to the player but expecting the player to go to settings to fiddle with configurations and key bindings is in itself a hurdle.

Possible fix: It is very hard to say, the game SNKRX is an obvious place to look at: maybe if the game was less about precise strategic gameplay and more about button mashing, the difficulty to control the worm would go down easier.

Failure 2: Visuals
I hit a brick walls with visuals. I'm not a very good graphic designer to begin with so the task of making the ground you go through look good was impossible to me.

People have managed (I'm looking at games like Pepper Grinder, see gif). But I just couldn't figure it out. So I fell back on this sub-Limbo esthetic. It works for a free early access game but I would never have found the will to sell a game in such a state.

Even if I could pay an artist to do this work, it's still tricky: it's easy to commission a static background but how do you commission the entire way worms appear underground? It's no longer a graphic design task where you just output pngs, you probably need to experiment in the engine. 

It's possible but it is much more difficult, failure prone and expensive.

https://shared.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/2076580/extras/GrittyGameplay.gif?t=1728951730

Possible fix: Collaborate with an artist and spend sometime iterating visuals. That's straightforwardly the solution but this was just not an option

Failure 3: Lack of variety
A roguelike lives or dies on variety and sadly I could not produce it in this game. 

I has assumed that I would be able to come up with a ton of different weapons but i ended up with five or so weapon types with a few different levelled up versions. There are more weapons than that but the other ones are barely worth ever picking up.

The end result is a roguelike that you will finish in about 2 hours and probably not come back to.

The partial solution was the upgrade system: at regular interval throughout the run, you get stat upgrades. But the game still fell short even with them.

At the end of the day, there is only so many things you can do that fit into the "lateral worm cannon" mold. I've done seeking missile, cannon, gattling, laser, grenades. What else is there that wouldn't largely overlap with these?

Possible fix: One lateral solution would have been to make more encounter variety: instead of only fighting worms there would be different enemy types. That could create more varying runs where the choices of weapons could have more influence on the run.

Conclusion
For all these reasons and some further personal ones, this game will never be fully finished.

But I do hope that someone does explore this idea again some day. I doubt they will ever come across this post but who knows. I wish them luck nonetheless.

In the end, I do believe that the only hurdle to people making good art is time and room to fail. I'm infinitely grateful that I was granted both to try and make this game.

Thanks for reading through this and please consider checking out my new game: The people of Sea, Sun & Salt

notes.title: Update #4: How to best steer a worm
notes.content:
This is a small update on balancing and control. The single biggest hurdle for this game is definitely the movement system: I've seen a lot of people say the game is fun or interesting but the controls are hard to grasp if not downright bad. So I added a toggle to pick between two modes of Juggernaut control. 

Changes:

- Players can pick between two ways of steering the Juggernaut: left/right steering or direction steering

- Rehearsal enemies have less health, Execution enemies have more health

- Seeker weapon deal less damage

- Rail cannon, cannons, volley and bomber weapons deal more damage

- Enemy weapon cooldown is slightly longer

- Fixed an issue where some early levels couldn't be completed when in windowed mode

Future changes

To further improve controls, I'll add key rebinding soon. Maybe that will help with players having issues with controls.

notes.title: Update #3: The one where I cave
notes.content:
Given player feedback and the small number of players reaching the top, I've decided to create two difficulty modes:
- The Rehearsal: Falls only do a little damage before bouncing you back up and enemies have less HP
- The Execution: Falls are lethal and enemies have a bit more health

I always liked the purity of having a single main mode and forcing players to just get better through sheer repetition but I think that is too strong a filter for players. So if I want to keep an expert level experience in the end game, two difficulty modes balanced differently is the way to go.

Changes

- Two difficulty modes as mentionned above

- Soundrack variety: These are still placeholder for better commissioned work but at least it is a bit less repetitive

- New weapon: The one sided cannon: Shoots two cannon balls from the right side only

- Speedrun achievements are less difficult

- Final boss fight level improvement

- Avoiding the upgrade screen appearing at the same time as the death screen

- No arsenal upgrades after the last arsenal

Future updates

The game is getting closer and closer to a tight little roguelike with most bugs addressed and balancing on it's way to releasability. The next big hurdle is going to be commissioning art, sound design and possibly music. There might be less regular updates as I try to figure out how to both reach these different artists and finance these commissions.

A few players mentionned SNKRX so I had a look and I obviously see the similarity. It's not out of the question that I end up moving the game in that direction: more hectic, faster pace, easier controls but Iron Mandate might risk losing the skill element that makes it interesting. That being said, Iron Mandate can have some pretty low down times so I'll keep an open mind to ways of juicing the gameplay.

Also I've heard of players playing "Archon mode" where one player controls movement and the other controls weapons. That's fun :).

notes.title: Update #2: Versus and even more deadly falls
notes.content:
Iron Mandate v0.6.3 is here. I'm still mostly trying to ensure that the game is decently balanced and runs without any issues. Once that is done I'll contemplate bigger feature work. Thank you to everyone who have made suggestions on that last point, there are definitely some keepers there.

Changes:

- Versus is available again: Play against players locally or through Steam's Remote Play Together (open the steam overlay to invite friends)

- Mid air control: Mid air control is stronger now to be able to more easily maneuver and avoid deadly falls. 

- New upgrade: A mid air control upgrade that almost allows you to hover.

- Keyboard issues: Keyboard used to take a few milliseconds to stop turning after the end of a key press. Now it's instantaneous.

- Out of bound enemies: Enemies can no longer get lost out of bound on some of the later levels

- Introduced windowed mode and handled different resolutions better

- Fixed extra segment strength for the first arsenal

- Fixes with the Juggernaut icons not appearing properly when they go off screen

- A bunch of other small fixes not worth mentionning

Future updates:

Not too much is set in stone but one thing is for sure: I will be improving the musical selection soon. I like the saxophone kicking in during the Knight fight but it might not be to everyone's preference. 

I said I would look at keyboard key mapping but I didn't for this update. I still want to have a think about it. I think the "A/D + UIOP" control works ok but it is inconvenient when picking your upgrade so I'll try to figure how to improve that.

notes.title: Update #1: Controls, Missed upgrades and deadly falls
notes.content:
I'm very grateful to everyone who gave Iron Mandate a try! The amount of feedback that came in is extremely helpful and will get us much closer to completing this game.

Changes:

- Gamepad control: Now works on Xbox controllers with no extra configuration needed

- Keyboard control: Changed movement so A and D turn the Juggernaut left or right relative to it's current direction

- Missed upgrades: You can no longer leave a level before getting the upgrade and cogs

- Accidental level transition: You now need to go further on the edge of the screen to trigger a level transition

- Balancing: Turrets last 20% shorter and automatons have 10% less health

- Deadly falls: I'm still uncertain on how to handle falls so for now I just added a bit of midair control to be able to recover. 

- Stuck on the ground: This midair control also allows players to get unstuck if they fall on the unbreakable ground

- It's harder to get lost in the grass on the tutorial levels

Possible future updates:

Here's a few bits of feedback I saw but haven't yet tackled:

- Improving keyboard control: the controls are still not perfect on keyboard so I'll keep trying things out, I might even consider using the mouse to let the player point where they want the juggernaut to go.

- Consider having a shop reroll option

- Consider having an upgrade reroll option

- Enemies sometimes get stuck out of bounds. I'm not sure yet what levels are doing this but I'll keep looking.

- Enable customizable keyboard/controller button mapping

- Map a button to fire all weapons at once

- Increase the number of music tracks in the game

- Add sound design. Ideally, this would be done by a professional with funds raised later.

Feel free to let me know if you'd like to see any other changes. We will keep improving this game and hopefully we will get it to a point of completion where I can consider recruiting an artist to finish the visuals.

This is version v0.5.7
